info.title: Mintlify Databases API
info.description:
API for reading and writing Mintlify Databases.

**Addressing.** `{database}` is the database slug or its id; a slug never looks like a uuid. `{column}` is the column name, matched case-insensitively, or its `col_…` id; an unknown name answers 404 listing the column names. `{id}` is a record id.

**Scopes.** API keys carry a read or write scope; a key with no scopes has full access. GET operations need `read`; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE need `write`, except `POST /records/query`, `POST /sql` and `POST /events/session`, which only read and need `read`. Each operation also states its scope in `x-mintlify-scope`. The live events stream takes no API key: its session token is the credential.

**Idempotency.** `POST /` (create a database), `POST /records` and `PUT /records` accept an `Idempotency-Key` header. The first response is replayed for 24 hours; reusing a key with a different body returns 422 `idempotency_key_reused`.

**Concurrency.** Records carry a `version`, also sent as a quoted `ETag`. `PATCH` and `DELETE` on a record accept `If-Match` and return 412 `version_mismatch` when it is stale.

**Errors.** Errors from the databases API are `DatabaseError`s: `{ error, code, fields?, ...details }`. 400 means a malformed request (unparseable JSON, bad path or query parameter); 422 means a well-formed body that failed validation, with per-field messages in `fields`. The API-key layer in front, shared by every external Mintlify API, answers 401, 403 and its own 429 as `AuthError`s: `{ error }`, with no `code`. The per-organization rate limit answers 429 with a plain-text body.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 63 characters. A uuid can never be a valid slug.

DatabaseSummary.description: A database without its columns, row count or cursor. Get the database for those.

code.description: Machine-readable code. Known codes: invalid, unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, conflict, cursor_expired, version_mismatch, too_large, unsupported_media_type, idempotency_key_reused, rate_limited, upstream, unavailable, internal.

fields.description: Per-field validation messages, keyed by the path of the offending field

DatabaseError.description: Every error the databases API itself returns has this shape. Some codes carry extra details beside `error` and `code`, such as `cursor` on `cursor_expired` and `version` on `version_mismatch`. Errors from the API-key layer in front of it are `AuthError`s instead.

error.example: API key does not have the 'write' scope

AuthError.description: An error from the API-key layer shared by every external Mintlify API, which runs before the databases API: `{ error }` only, with no `code`. It answers 401 for a missing or invalid key or a plan without API or databases access, 403 for a key without the required scope or a request from outside the key's IP allowlist, and 429 when the key's own rate limit or usage is used up.

name.description: Column name, unique within the database

strict.description: Select types only. When false, writing a value that is not in `options` adds it as a new option. When true, such a write is rejected.

Column.description: Types: text, number, boolean, date (YYYY-MM-DD), datetime (ISO 8601 UTC), select, multi_select, url, email, json.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 63 characters. A uuid can never be a valid slug.

cursor.description: Opaque change cursor. Pass it back unchanged; do not parse or construct it. Change cursors are shared across `cursor` on a database, `GET /{database}/changes` and the `id` of each live event, so any of them resumes the others. This one is as of this read: pass it to `GET /{database}/changes` to receive every change made after it.

UpdateColumnBody.description: A column's type cannot change. `options` and `strict` are rejected on columns that are not select types.

additionalProperties.description: The value for the column's type: a string for text, url, email, select, date (YYYY-MM-DD) and datetime (ISO 8601 UTC); a number; a boolean; an array of strings for multi_select; any JSON value for json. `null` clears the field.

Fields.description: Field values keyed by column name

version.description: Increases on every write. Also sent as the `ETag` header, quoted.

updatedBy.description: Actor that last wrote the record

total.description: Present when the query set `count: true`

column.description: Column name, matched case-insensitively, or its `col_…` id

value.description: An array for `in`; omitted for `is_empty` and `is_not_empty`; a single value otherwise.

column.description: Column name, matched case-insensitively, or its `col_…` id

where.description: Filters, all of which must match

cursor.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page of the same query

count.description: Also return `total`, the number of matching records

id.description: Updates this record, or creates it with this id

VersionMismatchError.description: The record changed since the version sent in `If-Match`.

UpdateRecordBody.description: Merged into the record: fields you omit keep their values, and `null` clears one.

columns.description: Output column names, in select-list order

rows.description: One array per row, its values in `columns` order. multi_select and json values come back as arrays and objects, booleans as booleans.

truncated.description: Whether the server's row or size cap cut the result short

SqlPosition.description: Where in the query the problem is

SqlError.description: The query was refused. `position` points at the problem when it has a place.

query.description: One SELECT from `records`. Bind values with `?` and `params`.
query.example: SELECT "Plan", count(*) AS n FROM records WHERE "Signed up" >= ? GROUP BY "Plan"

params.description: Values for the `?` placeholders, in order; at most 100

column.description: Set on column changes: the column's current name, or its `col_…` id when the column has been deleted since (always so for `column.deleted`).

version.description: Record version after the change, set on record changes

cursor.description: The cursor after the last change returned, or the one sent when there were none. Pass it to the next request. A page holds at most 500 changes, so keep calling until `changes` is empty.
The current change cursor to resume from, after re-reading the data

CursorExpiredError.description: The cursor expired or belongs to another database; resume from `cursor`.

url.description: The Server-Sent Events endpoint, `https://api.mintlify.com/api/external/v1/databases/events?token=…`, with `token` already in its query string so a browser `EventSource` can open it without an API key. Append `&cursor=` with a change cursor to receive only the changes after it.

token.description: The signed token that is `url`'s only credential: read-only, for this one database, valid for 5 minutes. It is checked when the stream opens.

expiresAt.description: When `token` stops opening streams, 5 minutes after the session started

cursor.description: The latest change cursor when the stream opened

ReadyEvent.description: The first event. Changes after the requested cursor follow it, oldest first, then live changes as they happen.

id.description: The change cursor of this change; resume after it with `Last-Event-ID`

ChangeEvent.description: One change, in the same shape as `/changes` returns

id.description: The cursor at the start of the current log

ResetEvent.description: The requested cursor cannot be continued from, for one of two reasons: the change log restarted under a new epoch (which is also how a cursor from another database looks), or the cursor fell out of retained history, which keeps the 10,000 most recent changes. Changes may have been missed, so re-read the data. The stream then replays every retained change from the oldest and carries on live.

cursor.description: The cursor after the last change sent; reconnect with it

ReconnectEvent.description: The stream reached its time limit, about 5 minutes, and is closing. Reconnect from `cursor`, with a new session once the token has expired.

data.description: An `upstream` error. The storage backend's own error is never relayed.

ErrorEvent.description: The stream failed and is closing. Reconnect from the last event id received.

LiveEvent.description: One Server-Sent Events frame: `event: <event>`, then `id: <id>` when it has one, then `data: <data as JSON>`. While nothing changes, a `: heartbeat` comment line arrives about every 20 seconds; `EventSource` ignores it.

post.description:
`fields` maps columns to values. Key each field by the column name, in any case, or by its `col_…` id; an unknown column is refused with 422 listing the column names, and so are two keys for the same column. Each value must suit its column type (see `Fields`), and `null` or an omitted field leaves it empty, which a required column refuses with 422.

Writing a value that is not among a select or multi_select column's `options` adds it as an option, unless the column is `strict`, which refuses it with 422. A column holds at most 200 options.

The response carries the new record and its version as a quoted `ETag`, ready to send back in `If-Match`.

Requires the `write` scope.

post.description:
Runs one read-only `SELECT` over the database, for questions filters cannot express: aggregates, grouping and ranges. It reads only, so it needs just the `read` scope.

- **One table.** Select from `records`, optionally aliased. Joins, subqueries, CTEs, `UNION`, window functions, other tables, other statements and comments are refused.
- **Columns by name.** Reference a column by its name in any case, quoted with `"…"` when it has spaces, or by its `col_…` id. `id`, `version`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by` and `updated_by` are there too.
- **Clauses.** `DISTINCT`, `WHERE`, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT` and `OFFSET`, with comparison, boolean and arithmetic operators, `IN`, `BETWEEN`, `IS NULL`, `LIKE`, `CASE` and `CAST`.
- **Functions.** Aggregates (`count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `total`, `group_concat`) and `lower`, `upper`, `length`, `substr`, `trim`, `ltrim`, `rtrim`, `replace`, `instr`, `coalesce`, `ifnull`, `nullif`, `abs`, `round`, `date`, `time`, `datetime`, `julianday`, `strftime`, `typeof`, and `has(column, value)` for multi_select membership. Any other function is refused.
- **Limits.** Without a `LIMIT`, at most 100 rows come back; with one, at most 1,000. `truncated` says when the cap cut the result. Bind values with `?` and `params` (at most 100).

A refused query answers 422 `invalid`, with `position` when the problem has a place in the query.

Requires the `read` scope.

get.description:
Returns changes made after `cursor`, oldest first, and a cursor to continue from. A call returns at most 500 changes and takes no `limit`; call again with the returned cursor until `changes` is empty.

`cursor` is required, and a request without one returns 400 `invalid`. To receive only changes made from now on, start from the database's `cursor` (`GET /{database}`). To replay the whole retained history instead, open the live events stream without a cursor.

Cursors are opaque. The database's `cursor`, the cursor this returns and the `id` of each live event are the same kind of value, so any of them works here and as `Last-Event-ID`.

A change names its column by the column's current name; a column deleted since keeps its `col_…` id, as `column.deleted` always does.

Only the 10,000 most recent changes of a database are kept. A cursor that has fallen out of that history, or that belongs to another database or to a change log that has since restarted, returns 409 `cursor_expired` with the current cursor; re-read the data and continue from that cursor. A value that is not a change cursor at all returns 400 `invalid`.

Requires the `read` scope.

post.description:
Returns a Server-Sent Events `url` for this database and the token in it. Opening a session reads only, so it needs just the `read` scope.

- **Token.** Signed, read-only, for this database alone, and valid for 5 minutes. It is the stream's only credential, so the stream takes no API key and a browser `EventSource` can open `url` directly. An expired, altered or unknown token, or one whose database was deleted, gets 401 `unauthorized`. Start a new session to reconnect after `expiresAt`.
- **Where to start.** Append `&cursor=` with a change cursor, such as the database's `cursor`, to receive only later changes. `Last-Event-ID`, which `EventSource` sends when it reconnects, takes precedence. With neither, the stream replays every retained change (the 10,000 most recent) before live ones.
- **Events.** See `GET /api/external/v1/databases/events` for the stream and each event.

get.description:
Streams one database's changes as Server-Sent Events. Open the `url` from `POST /{database}/events/session`, which already carries `token`; a browser `EventSource` can open it directly.

- **Credential.** `token` is the only credential: the stream takes no API key and no scope. It is checked when the stream opens, so an open stream outlives `expiresAt`, but reconnecting after it needs a new session.
- **Where to start.** The stream sends the changes after `Last-Event-ID`, else after `cursor`, then live changes as they happen. With neither, it replays every retained change (the 10,000 most recent) first; to receive only new changes, start from the database's `cursor`.
- **Events.** `ready` (`{ cursor }`, the latest cursor) opens the stream. Each `change` carries a `Change` and has its change cursor as the event `id`.
- **`reset`** (`{ cursor }`, also its `id`) means the requested cursor cannot be continued from, for one of two reasons: the change log restarted under a new epoch, or the cursor fell out of retained history. Changes may have been missed, so re-read the data; every retained change is then replayed from the oldest.
- **`reconnect`** (`{ cursor }`) means the stream reached its time limit, about 5 minutes: reconnect from `cursor`. **`error`** (a `DatabaseError` with `upstream`) means the stream failed: reconnect from the last event `id`. Both close the stream.
- **Heartbeats.** While nothing changes, a `: heartbeat` comment line arrives about every 20 seconds.

Errors before the stream opens are JSON `DatabaseError`s, except the plain-text 429.

schema.description: The `token` from `POST /{database}/events/session`, already in its `url`. It is the only credential: send no API key.

A change cursor to resume after, such as the database's `cursor`; `Last-Event-ID` wins when both are sent. Without either, the stream replays every retained change (up to the 10,000 most recent) before live ones, so start from the database's `cursor` to receive only new changes.
The `id` of the last event received, which `EventSource` sends by itself when it reconnects. It is a change cursor and takes precedence over `cursor`.

200.description: The event stream. Each frame is one `LiveEvent`: `event`, `id` when it has one, and `data` as JSON.

400.description: `cursor` or `Last-Event-ID` is not a change cursor (`invalid`)

401.description: The token is missing, altered, expired or unknown, or its database was deleted (`unauthorized`). Start a new session.

429.description: More than 120 streams opened in a minute for the token's organization. The body is plain text.
